target: Στο χωριό παντρεύονται νέοι ακόμα.
english: In the village they still marry young.
tip: παντρεύονται (pandrevonde) looks passive but means plain 'they marry'. Some verbs exist only in the -ομαι family – marrying is one of them.

target: Είμαι ερωτευμένη μαζί του.
english: I'm in love with him.
tip: ερωτευμένος/-η (erotevménos) = in love — the adjective, agreeing with the speaker.

target: Σκέφτομαι να του το πω απόψε.
english: I'm thinking of telling him tonight.
tip: σκέφτομαι να (skéftome na) = think of doing — 'να' plus the verb, not the infinitive.

target: Μας σύστησαν κοινοί φίλοι.
english: Mutual friends introduced us.
tip: Object pronouns go before the verb: μας σύστησαν (mas sistisan) = literally 'us they-introduced'. Short pronouns always sit ahead in Greek.

target: Η μαμά και η αδερφή μου μαλώνουν συνέχεια.
english: My mom and my sister argue all the time.
tip: μαλώνω (malóno) = to argue/quarrel — also 'to scold' when it takes an object.

target: Τα αδέρφια μοιάζουν πολύ μεταξύ τους.
english: The siblings look a lot alike.
tip: μεταξύ τους (metaxi tous) is literally 'between them' – Greek for 'each other': μοιάζουν πολύ μεταξύ τους (miazoun poli metaxi tous) = they look a lot alike.

target: Η κόρη μου μοιάζει στον παππού της.
english: My daughter takes after her grandfather.
tip: μοιάζω σε (miazo se) = resemble TO someone: μοιάζει στον παππού (miazi ston pappou) = takes after her grandfather. The σε is required – no direct object.

target: Δεν αντέχω όταν φωνάζουν στο σπίτι.
english: I can't stand it when they shout at home.
tip: δεν αντέχω (den andecho) = I can't bear it – stronger than δεν μπορώ (den boro), the plain 'I can't'. αντέχω is about endurance running out.

target: Έχουμε μια πολύ δεμένη οικογένεια.
english: We have a very close-knit family.
tip: δεμένη (demeni) is literally 'tied': δεμένη οικογένεια (demeni ikogenia) = close-knit family. Greek ties families together where English knits them.

target: Η νύφη τα πάει καλά με την πεθερά.
english: The bride gets along well with her mother-in-law.
tip: The τα (ta) in τα πάει καλά (ta pai kala) = 'gets along' points at nothing – it's a built-in dummy 'them'. Several Greek idioms carry this silent τα.

target: Είπε κάτι και το πήρα στραβά.
english: He said something and I took it the wrong way.
tip: το παίρνω στραβά (to pérno stravá) = take it the wrong way — 'στραβά' = crookedly.

target: Ας τα βρούμε επιτέλους.
english: Let's finally make up.
tip: ας τα βρούμε (as ta vroume) = literally 'let's find them' = let's make up. The τα (ta) refers to nothing specific – another idiom built on a dummy 'them'.

target: Αξίζει να δώσουμε άλλη μια ευκαιρία.
english: It's worth giving another chance.
tip: αξίζει να (aksízi na) = it's worth — impersonal, followed by 'να'.

target: Έδωσα το χέρι μου και τελείωσε.
english: I offered my hand and it was over.
tip: δίνω το χέρι (ðíno to çéri) = to shake hands/make up — a gesture of peace.

target: Φοβήθηκα ότι θα σε χάσω.
english: I was afraid I'd lose you.
tip: φοβήθηκα (fovithika) looks passive but just means 'I got scared'. Feeling verbs take this -θηκα past: λυπήθηκα (lipithika) = I felt sad.

target: Ενδιαφέρομαι για το πώς νιώθεις.
english: I care about how you feel.
tip: English is interested IN something – Greek uses 'for': ενδιαφέρομαι για (endiaferome gia) = I care about. The για (gia) is fixed with this verb.

target: Χαιρόμουν κάθε φορά που σε έβλεπα.
english: I was glad every time I saw you.
tip: χαιρόμουν (cheromoun) is the ongoing past: I was glad, again and again. It pairs naturally with κάθε φορά (kathe fora) = every time – repetition takes this tense.

target: Μου αρέσει πολύ το ρεμπέτικο.
english: I really like rebetiko.
tip: The verb agrees with the thing liked: το ρεμπέτικο (to rebetiko) is one thing, so μου αρέσει (mou aresi) stays singular – 'it pleases me'.

target: Ακούμε λαϊκά τραγούδια στην ταβέρνα.
english: We listen to laika songs at the taverna.
tip: λαϊκά (laiká) = popular folk songs — the ϊ has a dieresis, so λα-ϊ-κά, three syllables.

target: Ο Θεοδωράκης έγραψε έντεχνη μουσική.
english: Theodorakis wrote entechno music.
tip: έντεχνο (éndechno) = 'art' popular song — a whole Greek genre, roughly 'refined pop'.

target: Αγαπάω τη φωνή αυτής της τραγουδίστριας.
english: I love this singer's voice.
tip: τραγουδίστρια (traɣuðístria) = female singer — the -ίστρια ending marks the feminine.

target: Το λαϊκό γλέντι κράτησε μέχρι το πρωί.
english: The folk feast lasted until morning.
tip: γλέντι (ɣléndi) = feast/revelry with music and dance — central to Greek nightlife.

target: Χορεύαμε ζεϊμπέκικο δίπλα στο τραπέζι.
english: We were dancing zeibekiko by the table.
tip: ζεϊμπέκικο (zeibékiko) = a solo, improvised men's dance — a rebetiko staple.

target: Μου αρέσουν τα τραγούδια με βαθύ νόημα.
english: I like songs with deep meaning.
tip: Liking many things makes the verb plural: τα τραγούδια (ta tragoudia) are plural, so it's μου αρέσουν (mou aresoun) – 'they please me'.

target: Σιγοτραγουδάω πάντα αυτό το ρεφρέν.
english: I always hum this chorus.
tip: σιγοτραγουδάω (siɣotraɣuðáo) = to hum — literally 'sing softly', one word.

target: Το συγκρότημα ανεβάζει νέο τραγούδι αύριο.
english: The band drops a new song tomorrow.
tip: ανεβάζω (anevazo) means 'raise' – online it means release: ανεβάζει νέο τραγούδι (anevazi neo tragoudi) = drops a new song. New music gets 'raised' onto the internet.

target: Στο τέλος ακούσαμε το αγαπημένο μου κομμάτι.
english: At the end we heard my favorite track.
tip: κομμάτι (komáti) = a piece/track of music — also just 'a piece' of anything.

target: Πάμε στο θερινό σινεμά απόψε;
english: Shall we go to the open-air cinema tonight?
tip: θερινό σινεμά (therino sinema) = the open-air summer cinema – outdoor screenings are a beloved Greek summer ritual, not a novelty.

target: Ο κινηματογράφος ήταν γεμάτος κόσμο.
english: The cinema was packed with people.
tip: Κόσμος (kosmos) means both 'world' and 'people' – γεμάτος κόσμο (gematos kosmo) is literally 'full of world', Greek's normal way to say packed with people.

target: Παρακολουθήσαμε ένα ντοκιμαντέρ για τη θάλασσα.
english: We watched a documentary about the sea.
tip: Παρακολουθήσαμε (parakolouthisame) comes from παρακολουθώ (parakoloutho = watch/follow) – the verb for shows and documentaries, a step more formal than plain βλέπω (vlepo).
